correctness.rationale: Exact coefficient identity T_g=DB with a compact diagonal gives the upper bound; finite-variable Hardy multiplier norm equals the torus supremum. A finitely supported near-maximizer and a conflict graph of uniformly bounded degree supply at least cR pairwise disjoint multiplicative translates, giving a uniform min–max lower bound on an n-dimensional subspace. Sending n to infinity and then the norm-approximation tolerance to zero proves the full limit; all quantifiers and index shifts are explicit. The exact example is a quadratic completion of a square. Embedded checker passed 194050 finite diagnostics but is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural and widely studied family of compact but non-Schatten Volterra operators receives a complete first-order singular-value asymptotic with a computable symbol-dependent coefficient for every polynomial. Arithmetic collisions among multiplicative frequencies make the coefficient genuinely phase-sensitive: a three-term example has exact constant (8/sqrt(3))log2 rather than the coefficient-modulus sum 6log2. The theorem supplies sharp approximation-number calibration, not a routine bound or isolated tabulation.
